evidence.observation: The baseline is recorded as "A SQLite cursor is rejected by api.check.", establishing that the existing supported boundary refuses a foreign DB-API cursor, yet no later section names the entry point that will admit a DuckDB snapshot.

The DB2 exit criterion is "Bind named fact roles to a read-only DuckDB snapshot and check uniqueness, inclusion and mandatory participation." with no statement of whether api.check admission is extended or a new binding component is introduced; §9 only says to "record the public entry point and result" per phase without proposing one.

concerns.recommendation: Name the public boundary for DB2/DB3 in the plan (extend api.check admission for a read-only DuckDB snapshot, or add a dedicated binding component), state which existing refusal it replaces, and make that entry point plus its refusal the DB2 acceptance pair so the gate is observable rather than inferred.
concerns.title: No admission path named for DuckDB snapshots despite a recorded api.check refusal

evidence.observation: "Use a read-only engine transaction." is stated as a binding rule with no mechanism: no connection access mode, no attached read-only database, no transaction-level flag, and no requirement to verify that a write or DDL statement against the snapshot is refused.

The same sentence "Use a read-only engine transaction." is repeated verbatim as the sole control, so the plan's only safety guarantee for the database side is an unqualified assertion; §0's "test both sides of every refusal" is never tied to a write attempt.

concerns.recommendation: Specify that read-only is established when the DuckDB connection is constructed (engine access mode / read-only database file), forbid reuse of a caller-supplied read-write handle, and add a required test that an INSERT/UPDATE/DDL attempt against the bound snapshot is refused, with the passing and refusing sides both recorded per §0.
concerns.title: Read-only guarantee has no enforcement mechanism and no refused-write test

evidence.observation: "Compare native and database verdicts over the same records, including missing tables, uncovered roles and bounded source keys." defines no equality relation between the two verdicts.

"Compare verdict, affected binding and coverage; compilation alone cannot discharge this gate." requires comparing affected bindings but does not say whether counterexample sets must match as ordered sequences or as canonicalized sets; SQL result ordering is not guaranteed and native iteration order is implementation-defined, so bindings can differ with no behavioural divergence.

concerns.recommendation: Define DB3 parity explicitly: verdict equality, plus set equality over canonicalized binding tuples with a stated tiebreak and sort key, and enumerate which observed differences count as parity failures versus tolerated presentation differences.
concerns.title: DB3 backend parity has no defined equality relation for verdicts or bindings

evidence.observation: The column is headed "Observable exit criterion" but the DB1 cell reads "Compile a guarded existential over a joint assignment and expose violating antecedent bindings.", which is a verbatim copy of the §2 proposed-behavior sentence rather than an observation with inputs and expected outputs.

"The [first draft spec](phase-DB1-spec.md) expands DB1." delegates the only concrete DB1 gate to a document that is not part of the reviewed bytes, and §9's DB1 verification is likewise "Run the first spec's focused selection and retain its verbatim pytest summary."

concerns.recommendation: Restate each §4 exit criterion as an observation (fixture or issue reproduction, entry point, expected verdict and expected refusal), and either attach the DB1 gate text or summarize it in the plan so the reviewed bytes alone establish what discharges DB1.
concerns.title: §4 exit criteria restate proposed behavior and DB1's only gate sits in an unreviewed spec

evidence.location: §0 Binding design rules / §6 Risks and controls
evidence.observation: "Bound counterexample rows independently of scan size." appears in both sections with no numeric cap, no engine memory or thread limit, no statement timeout and no spill/temp-directory policy.

"Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply." makes limits an observation to record rather than an enforced bound, so no stated control stops an unbounded scan or result materialization.

concerns.recommendation: Name the counterexample row cap and the engine resource limits (memory, threads, timeout) as configurable constants with defaults, state where they are set, and require a test in which exceeding a limit produces the recorded refusal rather than exhaustion.
concerns.title: Counterexample and scan limits are asserted but never quantified or enforced

evidence.observation: "Native execution requires the supported optional backend in a suitable environment." names no supported version range for the backend or its adapter.

"Native backend claims require native execution." and "DB3 records engine and adapter versions and end-to-end parity" (as stated in §5) do not say whether DB3 tests skip, fail, or record an unmet gate when the backend is absent; a skipped selection still yields a pytest summary, so the gate could be reported as run without a database.

concerns.recommendation: Pin the supported backend version range in the plan, require the DB3 gate to fail or be explicitly recorded as unmet when the backend is unavailable, and require the retained summary to evidence non-skipped database-backed tests before parity is claimed.
concerns.title: No supported version range and no policy for a missing optional backend at the DB3 gate

evidence.observation: "also test missing projection, NULL, duplicate input and incompatible type" lists NULL and duplicates as separate cases and never tests their interaction, which is where SQL diverges: a UNIQUE constraint admits multiple NULLs and an inclusion predicate over NULL yields UNKNOWN rather than false.

"DB2 must choose an explicit NULL mapping and transaction identity before accepting relation bindings." defers the mapping to an open decision while the §4 DB2 exit criterion already claims uniqueness, inclusion and mandatory participation checking.

concerns.recommendation: Require the DB2 spec to fix the three-valued-logic resolution per constraint family before implementation, and add duplicate-NULL and NULL-in-inclusion cases to the §9 DB2 acceptance list so the native and lowered readings are compared on exactly those inputs.
concerns.title: NULL handling is deferred while uniqueness and inclusion gates already assume a mapping

evidence.observation: "including missing tables, uncovered roles and bounded source keys" introduces "uncovered roles" and "bounded source keys" as gate conditions; neither term is defined anywhere else in the reviewed bytes.

The DB3 exit criterion repeats "including missing tables, uncovered roles and bounded source keys." verbatim, and §9's DB3 cases cover good and bad populations only, with no case exercising a bounded source key.

concerns.recommendation: Define both terms operationally (what makes a role uncovered, what a source key is and what bounds it) or replace them with named conditions, and add a matching §9 acceptance case for each so the DB3 criterion is checkable.
concerns.title: "Uncovered roles" and "bounded source keys" are used as exit criteria but never defined

evidence.location: §3 Dependencies and artifact homes, first sentences
evidence.observation: "DB1 and DB2 can be developed independently after their respective gates; DB3 needs both." is asserted while the same section anchors the work to a single starting point, "Start with [src/gnd/export/pyrel_rules.py](../../../../src/gnd/export/pyrel_rules.py)."

"PyRel export currently refuses an existential consequent." identifies a refusal that DB1 must change on the same export surface DB2 binds relation roles to, with no shared-module boundary or merge order stated.

concerns.recommendation: Identify the shared lowering/export surface, state which contracts each phase may not modify, and either sequence the two phases or record an interface contract that lets them land independently without conflicting edits to the same refusal path.
concerns.title: DB1/DB2 independence is asserted although both phases touch the same export surface

evidence.location: §1 Scope, sources and authority, first sentence
evidence.observation: "Issue requirements come from [#327](https://github.com/vasiloglou/gnd-public/issues/327), [#330](https://github.com/vasiloglou/gnd-public/issues/330), including their proposed changes and reproduction examples." makes mutable external issue bodies the requirement source with no captured copy, revision or retrieval date in the milestone notes.

"For each later phase, use the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair" binds the acceptance evidence to that same external text, so a later edit to either issue silently changes what the gate accepts.

concerns.recommendation: Copy each reproduction verbatim into the corresponding phase spec with the issue URL and retrieval date, and have §9 reference the captured copy so the acceptance pair is reproducible from repository bytes alone.
concerns.title: Acceptance pairs depend on mutable external issue text with no captured copy

evidence.observation: "The component index identifies `export.pyrel_rules`, `check.service`, `check.constraint_families`. Its November 27 review flagged 105 descriptions older than their source; resolve contract details against code and tests." relies on an index the plan simultaneously reports as stale, assigns the re-derivation to no phase deliverable, and names no action to refresh the index.
"Implementation baseline 83cd4170." pins a baseline with no re-verification step if it moves before DB1 implementation begins, which matters given the reported index drift.

concerns.recommendation: Add to the DB1 spec either an index refresh action or an explicit rule that contracts are cited from code paths and tests rather than index descriptions, plus a baseline-drift step that re-runs the intake observations if the baseline changes.
concerns.title: Plan relies on a component index it reports as stale, with no refresh or drift step assigned

evidence.observation: "Run the first spec's focused selection and retain its verbatim pytest summary." requires retained evidence only for DB1; the DB2 and DB3 sentences specify what to compare but no retained artifact, format or location.

"Milestone closure requires a replay across phases, a disposition for each issue and an inventory of unverified claims." presumes replayable evidence that the DB2/DB3 verification text never requires to be captured.

concerns.recommendation: State the retained evidence for DB2 and DB3 (verbatim test summary plus the compared verdict/binding/coverage table) and where each record is filed, so the closure replay can be performed from the numbered records.
concerns.title: Evidence retention is required for DB1 only, leaving the closure replay under-specified

evidence.observation: The section is titled "## 3. Dependencies and artifact homes" but its body names only one source file and three index components; no home is given for phase specs, numbered records, tests or documentation.

"Each phase needs its own spec and owner ruling, implementation, focused tests, independent diff review, refactoring review and numbered record." lists six deliverables per phase without paths, while §5 names only "docs/reference/capabilities.md".

concerns.recommendation: List the directory paths for phase specs, numbered records, focused tests and documentation in §3 so every §8 deliverable has a stated home, or retitle the section to match its content.
concerns.title: §3 promises artifact homes but supplies none for specs, records or tests

response.summary: The plan is coherent in structure and names three phased gates, but as written the reviewed bytes do not yet make the DuckDB lowering or the native differential claim demonstrable: no admission path is proposed for a read-only DuckDB snapshot even though the intake baseline records "A SQLite cursor is rejected by api.check"; the binding rule "Use a read-only engine transaction" has no mechanism and no refused-write test; and DB3 parity has no defined equality relation for verdicts, bindings or counterexample order. Resource bounds, the optional-backend absence policy, NULL three-valued handling and several exit-criterion terms are asserted rather than specified, so the gates cannot be checked against observations.
